children: Sportsman’s Warehouse posted second-quarter net sales of $295.6 million for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026, a 0.6% increase year-over-year, and reported a net loss of $4.4 million (diluted loss per share $0.11). Adjusted diluted loss per share improved to $(0.08) and adjusted EBITDA for the quarter was $8.7 million; the company reiterated full-year 2026 guidance with adjusted EBITDA projected at $30.0–$36.0 million. Management highlighted inventory reduction and lower net debt alongside improved merchandising in Hunting and Shooting Sports heading into the back half of the year.
Revenue: Net sales of $295.6 million for the thirteen weeks ended August 1, 2026 (up 0.6% vs. prior-year quarter); twenty-six weeks net sales $551.7 million (up 1.6% year-over-year).
Gross profit and margin: Gross profit of $96.0 million, representing 32.5% of net sales in the quarter (versus $93.9 million, 32.0% in prior-year quarter).
Operating income (loss): Loss from operations of $(1.1) million for the quarter (loss from operations $(19.2) million for the twenty-six weeks).
Net income (loss): Net loss of $(4.4) million for the quarter (diluted loss per share $(0.11)); six-month net loss $(26.3) million (diluted loss per share $(0.68)).

Adjusted metrics: Adjusted diluted loss per share $(0.08) for the quarter; adjusted EBITDA $8.7 million for the quarter and $0.6 million for the twenty-six weeks. Company reaffirmed fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance of $30.0–$36.0 million and capex guidance of $20.0–$25.0 million.

Category performance: Same-store sales were flat for the quarter; Hunting and Shooting Sports grew ~6.7%, led by firearms and ammunition, while Optics, Electronics, Accessories and Other rose 1.0%; other categories declined, with fishing pressured by western U.S. drought conditions.
Inventory and working capital: Total inventory at quarter end was $399.0 million, down $44.5 million year-over-year, reflecting improved seasonal timing and inventory discipline.

Balance sheet and liquidity: Net debt reduced to $167.0 million; cash on hand $2.0 million and total liquidity of $105.0 million (composed of $103.0 million facility availability and $2.0 million cash).

Cost and margin initiatives: Management cited more disciplined inventory management leading to lower freight expense and a one-time tariff benefit contributing to a 50-basis-point gross margin improvement year-over-year in the quarter.

Operational posture: No store openings planned for 2026; company emphasized sharpening assortment, localization, in-stock improvements and investments in technology and store maintenance to drive customer relevance into the fall and holiday seasons.
